title: I generated one character three ways with Meshy: one mesh, eight parts, and a base mesh with separate gear
author: VictorBuildsApps
selftext:
I used a surveyor character to test three ways of building a game character with Meshy 7.1: one mesh, eight separately generated parts, and a base mesh with the gear generated separately. Both sides of the picture are the third build. The right side is after a texture repaint with Codex image gen and a cleanup pass.

Every build came from the same concept and got the same Auto-Rig Pro rig and test poses in Blender.

One mesh took 30 credits and 49 seconds. It looks fine standing, but the map case and pouches are fused to the coat, so they bend with the body. In a walk the map case rides the thigh at about 40 degrees.

Eight separate parts (body, coat, trousers, one boot, belt, scarf, map case, hair) took 240 credits. The single mesh looked cleaner at rest and in all four poses I compared. The parts build had mismatches at the neck, cuffs and scarf, holes, and cracks at the knees.

The third build was one generation for the body with its close-fitting clothes and no gear. I generated the map case and pouches from close-ups and built the strap, buckle and compass in Blender. I weighted the case and pouches to one bone, and the case held its shape in the test poses.

In the deep squat test the coat clipped into the pouches. Generating the body without gear also lost the ankle straps, so I added those back later. The whole test used 390 Meshy credits, including a redo of the base.

This is a work-in-progress test character.
